title: To the Deep and Back 往返深淵

image.alt: To the Deep and Back 往返深淵 banner

paragraphs: 冒險者們在昏暗的地下室依序醒來，發現自己的身體哪裡怪怪的。仔細一看，每名冒險者身上都有各自不同的殘缺之處。不過，如果沒有記錯……大家不是都已經死了嗎？
在冒險者的回憶中，他們受聘於布萊特沃斯家族，與他們安插的人手，人稱「魅影」的法內羅・懷特，一起入侵敵對的貴族希爾維羅姆家族宅邸。然而，在幾日探勘完成，預計入侵的前一晚，魅影趁著大家睡著時一一綁起，自己一人綁架了希爾維羅姆家所有的成員，帶到冒險者們藏匿的洞窟。在洞窟內，魅影將希爾維羅姆家虐殺完後，逐一將冒險者們肢解。
但此時，冒險者們確實的醒來了。在你們正中間的地上，有鮮血繪製的法陣。從當中深淵語的內容，冒險者們判斷這是個復活儀式，上面留有一段話：「醒來，你們還沒完成你們的任務」。冒險者們也發現被復活的自己，已經成了不死生物。
在一段時間的掙扎後，冒險者們發現地上留有一排腳印，從腳印可以依稀判斷是個成年人類，而且很有可能是個貴族。冒險者們隨著腳印，推開沒有上鎖的門，走上了樓。
冒險者們發現自己處在一座未曾見過宗教的祠堂內，空蕩蕩的，只有牆上有些觸手的裝飾。突然，他們看見一名人形生物從祠堂內走出門口。冒險者透過魔法，命令生物朝著他們走來。定睛一看，那隻生物竟然有著魚頭人身的外型，冒險者們過去未曾見過這樣的生物。透過魔法，他們成功和這隻生物溝通，然而他的名字難以用冒險者們熟知的語言呈現，因此他們以最接近的語句，稱呼他為阿巴努。
與阿巴努簡單溝通後，他答應帶冒險者們去見他會用通用語的老大。大家走在空曠的路間，一個人也沒見著。
一段時間後，冒險者們來到了一個聚落，其中除了他們停下來的房子有兩、三層之外，剩下的房子都只有一層樓。阿巴努推開門，讓冒險者們直接進入。
房子內深處的沙發上，一隻巨大的蛙人癱坐著。他看向冒險者們，以稀客稱呼他們。蛙人向冒險者們以通用語自我介紹，其名為霍布。霍布為冒險者們準備了餐點（枯葉、骨頭等看起來不怎麼美味，甚至不確定是否能稱為食物的東西）。在冒險者們的詢問下，他們得知自己的復活儀式，很有可能是現在住在霍布樓上客房的一名人類的傑作。除此之外，他們也從霍布身上得知，這裡是個稱為「深淵」的時空，與冒險者們生前所處的「物質時空」平行。

paragraphs.quote: 「平行的意思是同時存在，且互不干涉。」

paragraphs: 深淵內居住的生物中，有部分被稱為「深淵人」是被從物質世界抓來深淵的生物（除了人類外，偶爾也會有其他物種），而在深淵待久了後，他們會逐漸失去理智，成為深淵人。除了深淵人之外的物種，便簡單以「深淵生物」稱之。深淵生物具有可以自由穿梭深淵與物質時空的能力，深淵人與誤闖深淵的生物則無法。

冒險者們在得到霍布的許可後，便到二樓拜訪這名將他們復活的人類。與霍布所說的深淵人不同，這名人類看起來與冒險者們更接近。在自我介紹後，得知人類名為派蒂・希爾維羅姆，是甫被滅族的希爾維羅姆家族中倖存的人。經過派蒂的介紹，他們得知希爾維羅姆家族與深淵長期合作，取得不少資源和財富，但代價是每一代的希爾維羅姆家都需要有兩名子代住在深淵，一名是像派蒂這樣的「俘虜」，另一名則是如派蒂的弟弟岡瑟，由他們的父親與深淵人生出的子代（岡瑟的母親名為切斯塔）。
派蒂表示自己復活冒險者們，是因為想請冒險者們為他復仇，殺掉滅了他家族的魅影，但他為了復活冒險者們，已經將自己所有的資源用盡了，因此無法提供給冒險者們太多幫助。同時，因為無法真正控制冒險者們，派蒂在冒險者們面前，看起來似乎有點恐懼。他也向冒險者們道歉，自己在將他們搬回深淵進行復活儀式時，有部分器官有缺漏，因此復活的他們身上會有所漏缺。
派蒂也告訴冒險者們，如果要能穿梭回物質世界，他們體內必須要有三隻被稱為「巴坦」的蟲子。巴坦在深淵雖然很多，但要取得他們，幾乎都要依靠獵殺深淵生物或深淵人才能取得。另一種方法則是與深淵的商人交易，但常常交易的代價都要用自己的肢體去換。
冒險者和派蒂詢問了獵捕巴坦和能遇到商人的地方。首先，派蒂先介紹現在大家所處的地方為觸肢堡，霍布算是這裡的鎮長。其他派蒂所知的地方包含以下：

穆爾卡札：空曠的平原，有較多商人出沒；艾爾特雷茲沙漠：沙漠，有著鬼怪、獸人等生物出沒，但也有較精為算計的邪惡生物；沉沒迴響：沼澤，深淵生物多住在沼澤底下；烏曼尼頓：主要為深淵人居住的城市，裡面的奈瑟學士實驗室，是已知深淵內唯一可以成功自殺的地點（從物質世界被綁架到深淵的奈瑟學士，在這裡研發出了自殺的方法）；帕克提利克：深淵過去的首都，如今多為兇猛的野獸，可作為獵場；克勞辛頓：主要為有爪類的生物，但對深淵人十分不友善。
考量派蒂的身體狀況，冒險者們決定先休息一晚，隔天再請派蒂帶領他們去穆爾卡札與商人會面。
冒險者們充分休息後，便在派蒂的帶領下，先前往穆爾卡札。
空曠的平原，冒險者們在遠出看見了一名商人，身上背著厚重的行囊。商人友善的與他們打招呼，卻有種些微古怪感。商人列出了他願意做的交易，冒險者們尚不確定是否真的要交易。他們與商人提出較量看看的可能性，商人沒有拒絕，但看似不靈活的商人卻很輕易地擋下了刺來的匕首，讓冒險者們幾乎放棄了暗殺商人的主意。事後派蒂也表示這不是個好主意。
冒險者們又多與幾個商人詢問，每個商人提出的交易都有一些不同，冒險者們都先記了下來。
接著，冒險者們討論著先穿越沉沒迴響，到艾爾特雷茲沙漠去獵捕一些深淵生物回來。
走入幽暗的沼澤，冒險者們在派蒂的帶領下，每一步都很小心。然而，依然有出差錯的時候。一名冒險者意外將腳踏入沼澤深處，被底下的生物抓住了。冒險者們合力朝著看不見的生物攻擊，最終將被殺死的生物拽出時，發現是一名手持長矛的蛙人。因為知道蛙人身上可能有機會取得巴坦的腳，冒險者們便將他的屍體背在背後，繼續往前。
走了一陣子，冒險者們看見了一個矗立在沼澤中央的小木屋，不確定為何會有這一塊不被茂密的植被覆蓋的地方，就像沼澤中的綠洲，冒險者們抱著小心翼翼的態度，敲了敲門。
一名動作緩慢的老太太應門，邀請冒險者們進入他的小屋。在對老太太還抱有懷疑的情況下，冒險者們格外小心地進入。他們從狹小的一樓翻開地面的木板，走入意外寬敞的地下室，地下室傳來陣陣的茶香。
在冒險者們的詢問下，老太太名為綺綺，從小就在這裡長大。老太太遞給冒險者們茶飲，但因為茶的顏色十分濃，難免讓人有點起疑。在簡單調查後，冒險者們發現「茶葉」竟然是巴坦的腳！經過派蒂的認證，雖然和平常的巴坦腳有點不一樣（稍微大了一點，可能是因為經過烹煮的關係，或是可能是不同亞種），但應該和平常的巴坦腳一樣。
在冒險者們的請求下，綺綺決定為他們燉一鍋粥，但為了調味，她得上樓去採點調味料。一名冒險者便偷偷跟蹤他，以確保綺綺沒有在背後做奇怪的事。
趁著綺綺不在，冒險者們趁機探索地下室的空間，發現竟然有一間儲藏室，掛了不少隻，少說十隻以上的剛剛遇見的蛙人，有的已經被剖開，有的則十分完整。在驚詫動作緩慢的綺綺能獵捕這麼多隻蛙人的情況下，冒險者們也發現派蒂對於這名老人竟然能這麼輕易取得這麼多巴坦腳，似乎心裡有點不平衡。
樓上，跟蹤的冒險者看著綺綺在房子旁邊的兩座花園，採了花、香菇等，口口聲聲說著這對身體健康，味道很香，似乎沒有任何惡意，純粹是動作很慢而已，心裡有那麼點愧疚。
半小時後，綺綺終於回到地下室，開始專心烹飪她的粥。冒險者們也發現她竟然從櫥櫃中拿出一罐「調味料」，裡面似乎是滿滿的巴坦腳！對此，派蒂已經快要忍無可忍，但基於自己是客人的身份，還是不好說什麼。
粥煮好了，綺綺把粥遞給冒險者們後才發現忘了拿餐具。一名冒險者決定幫忙，卻在餐具櫃內看見了一頭死貓，讓他不知所措，但綺綺似乎對於這頭死貓沒什麼概念，卻也不顯得慌張，著實讓人感到奇怪。
粥吃完了，一名冒險者嚷嚷著想要吃南瓜粥，於是綺綺走入儲藏室，拿了一顆南瓜，繼續烹煮。
利用綺綺煮粥的時間，冒險者們請派蒂現場用他們在這裡取得的大量巴坦腳，實行合成巴坦的儀式。兩名冒險者成功讓合成出來的巴坦注入體內，也開始感受到巴坦在體內的爬行感。
冒險者們討論著是否要在這裡大量搜集巴坦腳，但因為派蒂不敢把握這裡的巴坦腳和平常的是否一樣，因此他們還是決定吃完粥以後先去外面再狩獵一些深淵生物。
離開了綺綺的小屋後，冒險者們繼續前行，預計前往艾爾特雷茲沙漠去尋找更多獵物。走在沼澤中，他們發現了一些潛藏的生物。為了把握能取得巴坦腳的各種可能性，冒險者們嘗試獵捕這些生物—除了先前抓過的蛙人之外，還有如小型魔像的生物，而在冒險者的要求下，派蒂也現場為他們進行提煉。
在沼澤中，冒險者們發現幾乎可以收集到足夠的巴坦腳，甚至不用特別再前往艾爾特雷茲沙漠，於是他們便開始嘗試注入第二與第三隻巴坦到體內，看看是否真的如派蒂所言，能回到現實世界去。
首先，迪娃成功的穿越了，便也穿越回來，和大家一起行動。
艾娃也穿越成功，但他選擇留在原地不回來了。
亂步在注入巴坦的過程中，因為沒有熬過巴坦的副作用，瀕臨死亡。但因為知道在深淵無法真正的死去，冒險者們便決定將亂步殺死，讓他再次重生。他們也發現能在這樣的過程中回收巴坦。
於是亂步在重生後，重新注入巴坦，別也成功得到回去現實世界的能力了。
最後，亨家決定留在深淵。對於奪去他身體重要部分的派蒂（僅管是無意），他無法接受，必須制裁。
至於回到現實世界的亂步，發現自己正站在希爾維羅姆家族的宅邸內一間房間。一個熟悉的身影正躺在床上呼呼大睡，那人便是魅影。在魅影醒來之前，亂步便將其處決，也算是為了他們的死去，進行了報仇。

The adventurers awoke one after another in a dim basement and immediately felt something wrong with their bodies. Each was missing a different part. But if they remembered correctly... had they not all died?

They recalled being hired by the Blightworth family to infiltrate the estate of their noble rivals, the Sylveromes, alongside the Blightworth agent Phanero Wyatt, known as “The Phantom.” After several days of reconnaissance, on the night before the planned attack, the Phantom bound the adventurers in their sleep. He abducted every Sylverome alone and brought them to the adventurers’ hidden cave. There, he tortured the entire family to death before dismembering the adventurers one by one.

Yet the adventurers had unquestionably awakened. A magic circle painted in blood lay between them. Its Abyssal script identified it as a resurrection ritual and included a message: “Rise, for you have not done your deed.” They also discovered that their revived bodies were now undead.

After struggling for some time, the adventurers found footprints crossing the floor. They appeared to belong to an adult human, most likely a noble. Following them, the group opened an unlocked door and climbed upstairs.

They emerged inside an empty shrine to an unknown religion, decorated only with tentacles along the walls. Suddenly, a humanoid creature walked toward the exit. An adventurer used magic to command it to approach. It had a fish’s head on a humanlike body, unlike anything they had seen. Magic allowed them to communicate, though its name could not be expressed in any familiar language. They called it by the closest approximation: Abanu.
After a brief conversation, Abanu agreed to take them to his Common-speaking leader. They walked through deserted roads without seeing another soul.
Eventually they reached a settlement where only one building rose two or three stories; all the rest had a single floor. Abanu opened the taller building and ushered them inside.

A gigantic frogfolk sprawled on a sofa at the back. Addressing them as rare guests, he introduced himself in Common as Hobb and served a meal of dead leaves, bones, and other things that looked neither appetizing nor necessarily edible. Their questions revealed that the human staying in Hobb’s upstairs guest room had probably performed their resurrection. Hobb also explained that they were in a space-time called “the Deep,” which existed parallel to the “Material Realm” where they had lived.

paragraphs.quote: “Parallel means they exist at the same time without interfering with each other.”

paragraphs: Some inhabitants of the Deep, called “Deepfolk,” were creatures abducted from the Material Realm—mostly humans, though occasionally other species. A long stay gradually stripped away their sanity and turned them into Deepfolk. Native species were simply called “creatures of the Deep.” Such creatures could freely travel between the Deep and the Material Realm, but Deepfolk and accidental visitors could not.

With Hobb’s permission, the adventurers went upstairs to meet their resurrector. Unlike the Deepfolk Hobb described, this human looked much like them. He introduced himself as Pattie Sylverome, a survivor of the recently exterminated family. Pattie explained that the Sylveromes had long cooperated with the Deep, gaining resources and wealth. In exchange, each generation had to send two descendants to live there: one a “captive” like Pattie, and another born between a Sylverome and a Deepfolk. The latter was Pattie’s brother Gunther, whose mother was named Chesta.

Pattie had revived the adventurers so they could avenge him by killing the Phantom. The ritual consumed all his resources, leaving him little help to offer. Because he could not truly control the adventurers, he seemed afraid of them. He also apologized that some organs had gone missing while he transported their bodies into the Deep, accounting for their incomplete forms.

To return to the Material Realm, Pattie said, each adventurer needed three insects called Bach’tahn living inside the body. Bach’tahn were common in the Deep, but obtaining them generally required killing creatures or Deepfolk. They could also trade with merchants, though the price was often one of their own limbs.

The adventurers asked where they could hunt Bach’tahn or find traders. Pattie first introduced their current location, Käppenburg, the Fortress of Tentacles, where Hobb served as a kind of mayor. Other places he knew included:

Murkaza: an open plain frequented by merchants. Elterez Desert: home to ghosts, beastfolk, and cunning evil creatures. Sinking Echoes: a swamp whose creatures mostly live beneath the mire. Umaniton: a city inhabited mainly by Deepfolk; its Maester Nether’s Lab is the only known place in the Deep where suicide is possible, after the abducted Maester Nether developed a method there. Pactilyk: former capital of the Deep, now a hunting ground filled with savage beasts. Klaucingtton: inhabited mainly by clawed creatures that are deeply hostile toward Deepfolk.
Considering Pattie’s condition, the adventurers rested for the night and planned for him to lead them to the merchants of Murkaza the next day.
After a full rest, the adventurers followed Pattie toward Murkaza.

On the open plain they spotted a merchant in the distance carrying a heavy pack. He greeted them warmly, though something felt slightly strange. He listed his available trades while the group debated whether to deal. They proposed testing his strength. The merchant agreed and, despite his clumsy appearance, effortlessly blocked a dagger thrust, nearly ending their thoughts of assassinating him. Pattie later confirmed that it would have been a terrible idea.
They questioned several more merchants. Each offered somewhat different bargains, which the adventurers recorded for later.
The group then decided to cross Sinking Echoes and hunt creatures in Elterez Desert.

Pattie led them carefully through the gloomy swamp, but mistakes remained possible. One adventurer stepped too deep and was seized by something below. The group attacked the unseen creature together and dragged out the corpse of a spear-wielding bullywug. Knowing its body might yield Bach’tahn legs, they carried it onward.

After some travel, they found a small wooden house standing in the middle of the swamp. They could not explain why this patch was free of dense vegetation, like an oasis amid the mire. Cautiously, they knocked.

A slow-moving old woman answered and invited them in. Still suspicious, they entered with great care. Lifting floorboards in the cramped ground floor revealed an unexpectedly spacious basement filled with the scent of tea.

The woman introduced herself as Chi-Chi and said she had grown up here. She offered the adventurers tea, but its deep color made them wary. Investigation revealed that the “tea leaves” were Bach’tahn legs. Pattie confirmed that although they differed slightly from ordinary specimens—somewhat larger, perhaps from cooking or because they came from another subspecies—they should function the same way.
At the adventurers’ request, Chi-Chi offered to cook a pot of congee but needed herbs from upstairs. One adventurer secretly followed to ensure that she did nothing suspicious.

While Chi-Chi was gone, the others searched the basement and discovered a storeroom containing at least ten bullywugs, some cut open and some intact. They marveled that the slow-moving woman could hunt so many. Pattie appeared resentful that she could obtain such quantities of Bach’tahn legs with ease.

Upstairs, the follower watched Chi-Chi gather flowers, mushrooms, and other ingredients from two gardens beside the house. She repeatedly said they were healthy and fragrant. She seemed genuinely harmless, merely slow, and the adventurer felt slightly guilty.

Half an hour later, Chi-Chi returned and focused on her congee. The adventurers saw her take a jar of “seasoning” from a cupboard, apparently packed with even more Bach’tahn legs. Pattie was near his limit, but as a guest said nothing.

After serving the congee, Chi-Chi realized she had forgotten utensils. An adventurer offered to help and found a dead cat in the utensil cupboard. At a loss, he watched Chi-Chi react as though she did not understand the cat’s presence, yet without alarm. It was deeply strange.
Once the congee was finished, one adventurer demanded pumpkin congee. Chi-Chi took a pumpkin from the storeroom and began cooking again.

While she worked, the adventurers had Pattie use the many Bach’tahn legs they had found to perform the ritual for synthesizing whole insects. Two successfully received the resulting Bach’tahn and began feeling them crawl inside their bodies.

They considered gathering Bach’tahn legs in bulk, but Pattie could not guarantee that Chi-Chi’s specimens were identical to normal ones. The group decided to finish eating and hunt more creatures outside.

Leaving Chi-Chi’s house, they resumed their journey toward Elterez Desert. In the swamp they detected hidden creatures. Seeking every possible source of Bach’tahn legs, they hunted bullywugs and small golem-like beings, with Pattie refining their remains on the spot.

They soon realized the swamp alone could provide almost enough legs, making Elterez Desert unnecessary. They began implanting second and third Bach’tahn to test Pattie’s claim that this would let them return to reality.
Diva crossed successfully, then returned to continue with the group.
Ava also crossed, but chose to remain in the Material Realm.

Ranpo nearly died from the side effects of implantation. Knowing true death was impossible in the Deep, the adventurers killed him so he would resurrect again. They discovered that this also allowed them to recover his Bach’tahn.
After reviving, Ranpo underwent implantation once more and successfully gained the ability to return to the Material Realm.
Hengjia ultimately remained in the Deep. He could not forgive Pattie—even if the mistake had been unintentional—for depriving him of essential body parts. Justice had to be served.
Ranpo returned to reality inside a bedroom at the Sylverome estate. A familiar figure lay asleep on the bed: the Phantom. Before the man awoke, Ranpo executed him, avenging all their deaths.
